small_guidance: The conv_transpose kernel is using 254 registers/thread, limiting occupancy to 16.6%. Reduce register pressure by: (1) moving the innermost `for ic in range(0, IC)` loop OUTSIDE the `kd/kh/kw` loops and accumulating in a GEMM-style tile, or hoisting `x_off`/`w_off` base computations out of the inner loop; (2) reducing BLOCK_OC to 16 or BLOCK_SP to 32 to cut live registers; (3) add @triton.autotune over {(BLOCK_OC=16,BLOCK_SP=64,nw=4),(BLOCK_OC=32,BLOCK_SP=32,nw=4),(BLOCK_OC=16,BLOCK_SP=128,nw=8)} with num_stages=2.
large_guidance: Rewrite as an im2col-style GEMM: for each output tile of shape (BLOCK_M output positions × BLOCK_N output channels), accumulate over a K-dimension of (IC × KD × KH × KW) using tl.dot. Use one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial-tile). Compute the gather indices for the input slice implicitly inside the K-loop with stride/pad math. This converts the current scalar FMA pattern (which the compiler currently spills heavily — 254 regs) into proper tensor-core / MMA-friendly matmul. Also switch input layout to channels_last (NDHWC) so the IC dimension is contiguous along K and loads coalesce. Fuse bias add in the epilogue. Keep the BN+submean as a separate fused kernel (already cheap at ~5%).
